notes: Check batch 2026-10-22-check-6: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, at head 192abf3 with uncommitted skill changes; every run has rc 0, a model_id matching its tier, and skill_hash 40c55876... which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so all runs are graded against the current text.

Rule list: the six ecto-phoenix.md rules plus the rule new to this case's index row, Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call (uncommitted in SKILL.md, no previous verdict). references/ecto-phoenix.md is unchanged since 0397dec (git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only SKILL.md and references/testing.md), so the six are graded to the 2026-10-22-b standard, including its reading of Keep migrations to schema changes: a separate script that uses MyApp.Blog.Post misses the case check, not the rule, which forbids schema modules only inside migrations (haiku-2 line 139: alias MyApp.Blog.Post).

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call: graded on the sentence "When an argument is a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines, or holds a call of its own, build it first under a name that says what it is, write it one field per line, and set each multi-line statement apart with a blank line." Read literally, the "or holds a call of its own" clause covers a one-line keyword list or map whose value is a call, and that is what decides haiku-2 (line 105: |> change(published_at: DateTime.utc_now()); line 159: render(conn, :show, post: Blog.get_post!(id))). An argument that is itself a call and not a map, struct or keyword literal (haiku-1 line 118 and sonnet-1 line 106: |> Post.publish_changeset(DateTime.utc_now(:second))) and an fn argument (Repo.transact(fn -> ...), sonnet-2 line 152 Ecto.Migrator.with_repo(Repo, fn repo -> backfill(repo) end)) are outside the rule's text and not counted; sonnet-2 names that value anyway (line 109: published_at = DateTime.utc_now(:second)).

Every multi-line map/struct/keyword argument in the four files, quoted: the audit-log attrs map is built under the name attrs, one field per line, with a blank line before the %Log{} |> Log.changeset(attrs) |> Repo.insert() pipeline, in all four runs (haiku-1 lines 123-128, haiku-2 lines 110-115, sonnet-1 lines 112-115, sonnet-2 lines 119-124). The only other multi-line keyword lists are the Ecto from/2 query clauses. The query macro needs those clauses as a literal, so they cannot be named themselves; they were graded by whether the query is named before the Repo call. haiku-1 (lines 79-85: query = / from p in Post, ... / Repo.all(query)), sonnet-1 (lines 70-76) and sonnet-2 (lines 72-79) name it, with a blank line before Repo.all(query), and haiku-1's backfill script does the same (lines 156-161). haiku-2 pipes an unnamed multi-line from(...) into the Repo call twice (lines 72-77 and 142-147). Those are counted under Write pipelines that start with a value, following the 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-21 grades that flagged from(...) |> Repo.all(); its verdict on the new rule rests on lines 105 and 159 alone. The controllers' render/3 calls take a short keyword of names in haiku-1 (line 174), sonnet-1 (line 157) and sonnet-2 (line 173). Result: haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 clean; haiku-2 violated.

The other six rules: 0 of 4 violated. All four runs cast only [:title, :body] and set user_id on the struct; three use assoc_constraint(:user), and sonnet-2 uses foreign_key_constraint(:user_id) (line 33). All four use Repo.transact/2, preload the author (sonnet-2 by join plus preload), keep the migration to add :published_at and show via Blog.get_post!/1 over Repo.get!/2. The backfills are a script on the "posts" table (haiku-1), a raw-SQL script (sonnet-1), a release task with raw SQL (sonnet-2), and a script over MyApp.Blog.Post (haiku-2), which misses that case check.

Other rules changed since 0397dec were checked for other_violations: no run uses defstruct (the new nil-default sentence); every module opens use, import, alias in that order (the new Open a module rule); no do: bodies (the rewritten do: rule); every with has two steps; no tests. other_violations found: haiku-2 starts two pipelines with from(...) (Write pipelines), and sonnet-2 writes fn repo -> backfill(repo) end where &backfill/1 fits (Use captures, unchanged since 0397dec). No public context function lacks @doc and every MyApp.Blog has @moduledoc.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all four because plain mix format adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As in the previous sweeps, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2, with the DSL calls (field, belongs_to, timestamps, from, add, alter, execute and others) in locals_without_parens, and all four pass. Nothing compiles because Phoenix and Ecto are not installed.
Transcripts show every run reading exactly SKILL.md and references/ecto-phoenix.md, then writing blog.ex in one Write call (the Haiku runs first made the folder with mkdir). No run ran elixir or mix.
